Harbor survey records

Each survey lists the depth at every mooring of the north and south quays, taken at low water by the harbor office's own launch and checked against the previous season's soundings before it is filed with the port authority.

MooringDepth at low water, in metres, as sounded from the launchChange since the previous season's survey, in centimetres
North quay 16.2 metres at the seaward end of the berthshallower by 14 centimetres after the winter storms

Soundings that differ from the previous season by more than twenty centimetres are taken again on the next low water, and both readings are kept in the record with the time and the state of the tide at each.

How to read a sounding

A sounding is the depth below the chart datum at the moment it was taken, corrected for the height of the tide.

Further surveys and archives

Older surveys are kept in the harbor office's archive room and can be read there on any weekday morning.
